purpose: three visual directions for user selection

concepts.title: A · LIVING DIORAMA
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished, wide 16:9 full-screen educational space game concept screen for children ages 7–12. This is a proposed art direction, not a screenshot of an existing product. Rich illustrated tactile game art, excellent composition, readable short typography. Warm ivory ceramic, charcoal machinery, muted gold, navy glass, cool blue water, soft upper-left light. A consistent charming small astronaut in an ivory suit and navy visor. No logos or NASA insignia. No app browser chrome, no dashboards, no SaaS cards, no long paragraphs, no giant gradient buttons, no generic emoji. Gameplay occupies most of the screen, with an instantly understandable physical action. The science headline is prominent and integral: exact text "MELTING IS ONLY THE FIRST STEP". Directly underneath in clearly readable smaller type: "Space-station water is treated and checked before reuse." This is a lunar teaching model, NOT real equipment or a promise of potable lunar water. Show ice -> warming -> treatment -> checking -> storage as a whimsical physical experiment; no drinking glass or astronaut drinking. Resource quantities are fictional game units. Resource labels must be clear, not cryptic: Air 65/100, Water 42/100, Power 75/100, Energy 80/100. Separate a small spendable badge "Research tokens 16" from a permanent learning book labeled "Research progress". The selected action's forecast reads "Water 42 → 54", "Power 75 → 69", "Energy 80 → 76", and "Tokens 16 → 18". A concise cost/gain key explicitly says "USE −6 Power  −4 Energy  −1 Token  ½h" and "GET +12 Water  +3 Tokens". Never display unlabeled percentages or mysterious glyph-only values. Keep headline, resource names, quantities, and one physical action legible. Main action text "Run experiment". Small model label "Teaching model".
Direction A: LIVING DIORAMA. A beautifully art-directed, tangible miniature isometric lunar laboratory diorama, with dimensional silver-gray lunar ground and a black star-dotted outer void. The large sculptural experiment sits on an exposed 1x1-style platform in the foreground, joined to a cream dome base and little greenhouse in the background. In the apparatus, a cutaway reveals 3 luminous ice pieces in a glass warming vessel, warm copper coils, a visible layered filter, a small separate sample-check chamber, and an output water tank. Illustrated cream annotation ribbons attach directly to each component: "Warm", "Treat", "Check". A floating magnifying cutaway lens reveals flow inside rather than a modal window. The astronaut is actively moving an ice container. Strong sense of discoverable toy-world space, lovingly detailed faceted 3D forms, restrained stars, premium game art. Upper-left supply HUD is a tiny rack of physically recognizable air cylinder, water reservoir, battery and suit-readiness gauge; each has fill plus its clear name and amount. Lower foreground uses curved resource transfer trails and a restrained cream forecast strip with the specified cost/gain and before-after quantities. The science headline dominates the upper center in editorial ivory type on the star-black negative space. Direction title is a small tasteful top-edge label "A · LIVING DIORAMA". At least 65% of the composition is actual illustrated playable world. Not a flat illustration or web form.

Direction B: INVENTOR'S WORKBENCH. A highly tactile close view of a lunar inventor's workbench: the beautiful machinery itself IS the interface. Large modular ivory, brass and navy parts on a dark-blue inset science work surface. A big ice hopper, transparent warming chamber, a removable gold-rimmed multi-layer treatment cartridge, a separate sample-check window, and a chunky storage tank all physically connect using short glass tubes and brass joints. One empty cartridge socket has a subtle ghost silhouette and a translucent hand/action cue showing which physical part to move; only one next action is emphasized. The player could pick up and snap real illustrated parts, not operate UI widgets. Fluid particles clearly show cause/effect through tubing. A faint outlined 'prediction' water level in the storage vessel previews the result before the machine runs. A detailed small astronaut is visible beside the bench edge for continuity. Science headline is a large beautifully lettered workshop placard upper center, with the fact directly below. Resources are actual labeled containers in a compact dock: Air, Water, Power, Energy, fill and exact counts; consistent separate research-token pouch and permanent learning book. The resource forecast is drawn on a little physical work order near the output, with exact USE/GET labels and the before-after quantities. Highest clarity of all 3 directions. Seamless illustrated environment, satisfying material contrast, uncluttered experimental toy, large delightful interactive objects. Direction title is a small top-edge label "B · INVENTOR'S WORKBENCH". Do not make a rectangular card-based UI or another pipe puzzle on a CSS panel.

Direction C: DISCOVERY ATLAS. A premium interactive illustrated lunar field atlas, a large physical cream scientific sketchbook spread over a dark star-map desk. Rich painterly gouache / softly rendered dimensional toy illustrations, elegant spacious storybook science, refined rather than preschool. The pages contain one large coherent PLAYABLE water experiment drawn as a dimensional pop-up cutaway, with sculptural ice, a transparent warming jar, a treatment cartridge, a sample-check window and a storage reservoir; annotation leaders and little evidence stamps connect cause/effect. The player is moving a real illustrated ice specimen between the page's observation, experiment and evidence areas, not reading cards. A small astronaut stands on the illustrated lunar pop-up terrain. The large learning headline and one-sentence fact occupy the top of the open pages, given very high priority. Clearly labeled page beats "Observe", "Try", "Explain" integrate naturally into the illustration. Successful evidence pieces form an illustrated fact badge in the right page margin; the knowledge record feels permanent and earned. Resources live in a consistent compact top-left physical supply roll with named cylinders, water flask, battery and readiness gauge, numeric fill counts and capacities. A separate token pouch and book make spendable tokens versus permanent research progress distinct. Resource forecasts and USE/GET figures are a clean stamped experimental receipt, directly linked by drawn arrows to the relevant containers. Mature warm paper, navy ink, amber brass, cyan water, green evidence marks. Direction title a small top-edge label "C · DISCOVERY ATLAS". No web-form controls, no dense textbook page, no long text blocks, no nested cards; the playable illustration dominates.
